analysis: The only changed range is SSDPrefixCache.evictOldestEntry: base lines 1771-1788, head lines 1772-1779. Base behavior: it guarded on hasSafeRoot, took the index.oldestEntries() snapshot and tried each victim through retireIndexedEntries. It returned 0 on externalChange, returned the freed bytes on the first nonzero retirement, and counted one eviction. Head behavior: it adds a !isClosed guard, which is stricter, then delegates to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:isClosed:) with a closure that still calls retireIndexedEntries([url]). It counts an eviction when freed > 0. retireIndexedEntries (base 1794-1804) is unchanged. It still takes removalLock, rechecks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot (closed state and epoch ownership), and reconciles on externalChange. Path construction still uses the HMAC-derived tag16 under config.root, so the T-041 leak #2 posture (HMAC names, DBK3 AAD) is untouched. Staging, TTL sweep, scan, durable-receipt and reservation-release paths (base 1256-2193) are outside the changed range. I reviewed them only for interactions and found no change. Relevance: T-041 mitigation (b) uses the box-wide LRU disk budget to bound the at-rest reuse surface and to protect availability (T-016). The new helper, SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, is not in the supplied evidence. Integration should verify four things: (1) it still iterates a bounded snapshot, so it cannot loop forever on undeletable entries; (2) it skips a valid-but-undeletable victim, so a newer entry can still satisfy the budget; (3) it stops and returns 0 on externalChange (or handles it equivalently), so reconciliation is not bypassed; (4) its isClosed callback aborts mid-loop without leaving the index inconsistent. If the helper returned 0 prematurely, the box-wide budget could fail to free space. That would weaken the T-041 LRU bound and hurt availability. This is unverified, so no finding is raised.
